title: An Efficient Hardware Accelerator Design for Dynamic Graph Convolutional Network (DGCN) Inference
problem: Designing high-performance and energy-efficient DGCN accelerators is challenging due to distinct requirements: GCN layers perform sparse-dense matrix operations with irregular memory access from unstructured graph vertices, while RNN layers use element-wise operations with predictable access patterns.
motivation: Dynamic graph convolutional networks are increasingly applied to temporal graph-structured data in machine learning, requiring efficient inference support.
method: E-DGCN uses reconfigurable processing elements to handle sparse-dense matrix multiplication (multiplying a mostly-zero matrix with a fully-populated one), general matrix multiplication, and element-wise operations (applying the same operation to each number) for both GCN and RNN layers. The chip's internal data routing adaptively adjusts to reuse data, keeping recently-accessed data close instead of repeatedly fetching from main memory. A lightweight vertex caching algorithm stores frequently-accessed vertices (individual points in the graph) nearby, exploiting the pattern that the same vertices are often accessed in bursts, reducing memory traffic.
key_novelty: The core idea is combining three techniques—reconfigurable hardware, adaptive data routing, and vertex caching—to handle both the irregular scattered memory access of GCN layers and the predictable sequential access of RNN layers.
contributions: Reconfigurable processing elements for diverse GCN and RNN computations
Adaptive dataflow interconnection design for improved data reuse
Lightweight vertex caching algorithm for temporal locality exploitation
2.2x speedup and 2.6x energy savings over existing DGCN accelerators
